challenges.name: stop-conditions-quiz
challenges.title: Which stop condition fires?
challenges.description: Two traces from the CodeDev support agent: a model that alternates between two lookups, and a repeated-call check that compares raw JSON.

questions.question:
Limits: maxSteps 20, maxSameCall 3 (stop when the same call is proposed 3 times in a row), maxNoProgress 3 (stop after 3 tool results in a row that were already seen in this run).

Trace of run support-8812 ("Which of my orders can I still refund?"):
step 1  find_orders {"email":"lan@example.com"}  -> orders of lan@example.com: o-1001, o-1003
step 2  get_order {"orderId":"o-1001"}          -> order o-1001: python-data, paid
step 3  get_order {"orderId":"o-1003"}          -> order o-1003: sql-basics, paid
step 4  get_order {"orderId":"o-1001"}          -> order o-1001: python-data, paid
step 5  get_order {"orderId":"o-1003"}          -> order o-1003: sql-basics, paid
step 6  get_order {"orderId":"o-1001"}          -> order o-1001: python-data, paid
...

Statement: "In this run the repeated-call check never fires; the run is stopped by the no-progress check, at step 6."
questions.explanation: True. The repeated-call check counts identical proposals in a row, and here no call follows itself: the model alternates between o-1001 and o-1003, so the count never goes past 1. The no-progress check looks at results instead: steps 1-3 each bring a new text, step 4 repeats step 2's result (1), step 5 repeats step 3's (2) and step 6 repeats step 2's again (3), which reaches maxNoProgress at step 6. The misconception is that a repeated-call check catches every loop; a model that cycles between two or more calls slips past it, which is why it is paired with a progress check and a hard step limit.

False. The three calls ask the same question, but JSON.stringify keeps the key order the model wrote, so step 1's key (userId first) differs from steps 2 and 3 (courseId first). The count is 1 at step 1, 1 at step 2 (new key), 2 at step 3 and back to 1 at step 4: the check does not fire at step 3. Models do not promise a stable key order, so the comparison needs a canonical form, for example keys sorted at every level before stringifying. The misconception is that JSON.stringify gives one string per value; it gives one string per object as written.

challenges.name: agent-stop-conditions
challenges.title: Stop conditions for the support agent loop
challenges.description:
The CodeDev support agent answers questions about orders, enrollments and lessons with three read-only tools. Its loop, runAgent(question, model, limits), only ends when the model gives a final answer, so a model that keeps calling tools keeps it running. Add stop conditions. A step is one call to model.next().

1. max_steps: before each model call, if steps already equals limits.maxSteps, stop.
2. final: a turn { "final": text } whose text is non-empty after trim stops the run with that answer.
3. no_final_answer: any other turn that is not a valid tool call stops the run: an empty or blank final, a missing or non-string final, a tool call without a non-empty string name. Model output is parsed JSON, so check its shape.
4. repeated_call: when the same tool call (same name and same canonical args: object keys sorted at every level) is proposed limits.maxSameCall times in a row, stop when that proposal arrives, without running the tool.
5. no_progress: progress means a tool result text not seen before in this run. After running a tool, if the last limits.maxNoProgress results in a row were all already seen, stop.

Tools never throw: problems come back as results starting with "error:" and count like any other result. runAgent returns { reason, steps, answer, partial }: answer is null unless the reason is "final"; partial lists every distinct tool result of the run in the order they first appeared.

Input (stdin, JSON): { "limits": { "maxSteps", "maxSameCall", "maxNoProgress" }, "runs": [ { "name", "question", "script": [turns] } ] }. The fake model returns one scripted turn per call and repeats its last turn when the script runs out. Output: a JSON array, one object per run: { "run", "reason", "steps", "answer", "partial" }.
hints: For each step, what has to be checked before the model is called, what right after its turn arrives, and what after the tool has run? Write the five conditions in that order before you write any code.

Look at three places in runAgent: the top of the loop (the step budget), the moment the turn arrives (is it a usable final or a usable tool call, and is it the same call as the previous step?) and the line after callTool (was this result new?). Two counters that reset - one for identical calls in a row, one for results without anything new - and a Set of results seen so far are all the state you need.

A similar check on other data: deciding whether two API requests are duplicates. { "q": "joins", "page": 2 } and { "page": 2, "q": "joins" } are the same request, so compare them after sorting the keys - also inside nested objects - and stringifying; arrays keep their order. For progress, a crawler that has fetched pages A, B, A, B, A has seen nothing new for 3 fetches in a row after the second B.
